---
 
## §4 — BODY PLAN VARIANTS
 
### Standard Bipedal (default)
Human body base. Apply §3 type rules and §1 species feature additions. No body plan modification needed.
 
---
 
### Kemonomimi / Minor Animal Features
**Applies to:** Eevee and all Eeveelutions (standard bipedal form), Pikachu, Raichu, Meowth, Persian, Growlithe, Arcanine (bipedal), Vulpix, Ninetales, Jigglypuff, Clefairy, Snubbull, and all species whose non-human features are limited to ears, tail, and minor markings.
 
**Formula:** Describe full human body first. Then append:
`Non-human features include [species] ears positioned on top of the skull — [ear shape: upright and pointed / large and rounded / long and drooping / specify], [ear color matching species palette], [ear size relative to head], [inner ear color if distinctive]. [Tail: shape, length, base position at base of spine, color and texture matching species palette, current state — raised/lowered/curled/wagging].`
 
**Critical rule:** Never default to Pikachu ears or Eevee ears unless the character IS Pikachu or Eevee. Every species has distinct ear shape — specify precisely.
 
**Eeveelution-specific notes:**
- **Vaporeon:** Bipedal. Fin tail attached at base of spine — `"fin tail [blue, semi-translucent, fin-edged], not replacing legs."` Specify dorsal fin ridge along the tail. Blue fin-like ear structures. Water-type rules.
- **Flareon:** Large fluffy rounded ears. Cream-colored mane collar at neck. Fire-red tail with cream tip. Fire-type rules.
- **Jolteon:** Sharp spiky yellow ears. Spiky fur collar at the neck. Lightning-bolt tail. Electric-type rules.
- **Espeon:** Slender forked tail. Smooth lavender fur-tipped ears. `"Small red gem set in the forehead."` Psychic-type rules.
- **Umbreon:** Black ears with yellow ring markings. Smooth black tail with yellow ring markings. Yellow ring markings on skin at canonical body locations. Dark-type rules.
- **Leafeon:** Leaf-shaped ear tips. Leaf-pattern tail with brown base and green leaf tip. Grass-type rules.
- **Glaceon:** Smooth ice-blue ear flaps folded close to the head. Diamond-tipped tail. Ice-type rules.
- **Sylveon:** `"Two ribbon-like feelers trailing from each ear and two from each wrist, pink and white, moving gracefully."` Fairy-type rules.
---
 
### Serpentine Lower Body
**Applies to:** Ekans, Arbok, Seviper, Snivy line (Snivy/Servine/Serperior), Dratini/Dragonair
 
**Formula:**
`Human female upper body from the waist up, merging at the waist into a long serpentine lower body — no human legs, no human feet, only a single continuous serpentine coil from the hips downward, [length] in total, covered in [scale color and pattern per species] scales. Non-human features include complete serpentine lower body below the waist, replacing both legs entirely with a single muscular snake tail. The tail coils [around her body / pooled beneath her / extended behind].`
 
- Never use "legs" anywhere in a serpentine Pokégirl prompt.
- Specify scale pattern and color from species palette separately from skin color.
- Regenerate if human legs are visible.
**Species-specific notes:**
- **Arbok:** Purple scales. `"Large hood-like scale flare at the upper coil just below the merger point, with [species] hood pattern markings."` Poison-type rules.
- **Seviper:** Black scales with red zigzag markings. `"Tail ending in a red blade-like scale rather than a rounded tip."` Poison-type rules.
- **Serperior line:** Smooth green scales with cream/yellow underbelly. Leaf-like scale flourishes at the merger point and tail tip. Grass-type rules.
**Gyarados (sea serpent variant):**
`Human female upper body from the waist up, merging at the waist into a long powerful sea-serpent lower body — blue fish scales, dorsal fins along the spine of the coil, pectoral fin-like protrusions at the merger point. Two long [blue/white] barbel whiskers trailing from the lower jaw. Tail end with large fan fin. No human legs.` Water-type rules.
 
**Onix/Steelix (boulder chain variant):**
`Human female upper body from the waist up, merging at the waist into a chain of [grey boulders / iron-grey metallic segments] forming a serpentine lower body — segments increasing in size toward the tail end, [rocky texture / metallic polished surface], the chain flexible and articulated. No human legs.` Rock/Steel type rules respectively.
 
**Rayquaza:** `Human female upper body from the waist up, merging into a long sky-serpent lower body — green scales with yellow ring markings at regular intervals, very long and trailing behind. Yellow-outlined facial markings on the human face.` Dragon-type rules.
 
**Zygarde (50% form basis):** `Human female upper body from the waist up, merging into a serpentine lower body formed from black and green hexagonal cell-pattern segments. No human legs. Green diamond marking on chest. Multiple small green dot markings along the serpentine body.` Dragon-type rules.
 
---
 
### Mermaid / Aquatic Lower Body
**Applies to:** Milotic, Primarina, Kyogre, Wailord, Wishiwashi, and fully aquatic species requiring humanoid adaptation.
 
**Standard formula:**
`Human female upper body from the waist up, merging at the hips into a [species] tail — [scale color and pattern per species], [fin type and placement]. Human waist joins at hip level.`
 
**Species-specific notes:**
- **Milotic:** `"Elegant iridescent scaled tail — cream with pink and teal iridescence, large fan fin at the tail end, ribbon-like pink fin protrusions along the length of the tail."` Water-type rules.
- **Primarina:** `"Large rounded pinniped-seal lower body merging from the hips, pale blue-white, with large flipper fin at the base. Pearl accessories. Long flowing hair with pearl ornaments."` Water/Fairy type rules.
- **Kyogre:** `Human female upper body from the waist up, merging at the hips into a massive orca-cetacean lower body — deep blue with white underside markings and red curved line markings at canonical locations. Large tail flukes at the base. Pectoral fin-like protrusions at the merger point flanking the hips. Powerfully built. Red eye markings beneath human eyes.` Water-type rules.
- **Wailord/Wishiwashi:** Cetacean/fish mermaid formula — scale to species palette and body size.
**Note:** Vaporeon uses the Kemonomimi section — bipedal with finned tail attached, not mermaid lower body.
 
---
 
### Equine Taur-Type
**Applies to:** Ponyta, Rapidash, Galarian Rapidash, Zebstrika, Blitzle, Mudsdale, Mudbray, Keldeo
 
**Formula:**
`Hybrid female figure: human female upper body from the waist up, merging at the waist into the body of a [equine species] from the neck and shoulder junction downward. Non-human features include complete equine body below the waist, with four unguligrade legs ending in [equine hooves — specify color per species]. [Equine] body has [coat color and texture per species]. Human waist joins at the equine neck and shoulder junction — not a human riding or standing beside a horse.`
 
**Species-specific notes:**
- **Ponyta:** `"Mane and tail formed from living flame, yellow-orange, equine body cream or white."` Fire-type rules.
- **Rapidash:** Same as Ponyta plus `"single spiraling ivory horn."` Fire-type rules.
- **Galarian Rapidash:** `"Pastel pink mane and tail, white coat, single spiraling horn."` Psychic/Fairy type rules.
- **Zebstrika/Blitzle:** Zebra stripe pattern on equine body. Lightning-bolt tail tip. Electric-type rules.
- **Mudsdale:** Heavily built draft horse lower body, brown with cream feathering at hooves. Ground-type rules.
- **Keldeo:** Blue-white equine body, colored mane and horn per forme. Water/Fighting type rules.
---
 
### Arachnid Body Plan
**Applies to:** Spinarak, Ariados, Joltik, Galvantula, Dewpider, Araquanid
 
**Formula:**
`Hybrid female figure: human female upper body, rising from the front and top of a large arachnid lower body. Non-human features include complete arachnid body below the waist — eight arachnid legs emerging from the arachnid body, human torso rising from the front and top of the leg cluster, not the rear. Large bulbous arachnid abdomen-tail protruding behind. Human torso faces forward, above and in front of the leg cluster.`
 
Never use "spider" — use "arachnid." Regenerate if human torso is positioned behind the legs rather than above and in front.
 
**Species-specific notes:**
- **Ariados:** Red arachnid body with yellow markings. Silk thread trailing from the abdomen-tail. Bug/Poison type rules.
- **Galvantula:** `"Arachnid legs covered in yellow and blue fur."` Compound eyes. Electric/Bug type rules.
- **Araquanid:** `"Large transparent water bubble enclosing the head and upper torso, the face visible through it."` Teal arachnid lower body. Water/Bug type rules.
- **Dewpider:** Same formula as Araquanid, smaller scale. Water/Bug type rules.
---
 
### Amorphous / Slime Body Plan
**Applies to:** Ditto (untransformed), Grimer, Muk, Alolan Grimer/Muk, Goodra, Sliggoo, Gulpin, Swalot
 
**Formula:**
`Humanoid female figure with a body formed from [color per species] [translucent / opaque / glossy] slime or gel — skin has a [wet / glossy / viscous] quality, [specify consistency per species], with the suggestion of the figure's form visible through or within the substance.`
 
**Species-specific notes:**
- **Ditto:** `"Body formed from purple translucent slime, features simplified and slightly unformed — large dot eyes, curved smile line, the rest of the face suggested rather than defined. Body takes approximate human female shape but edges are fluid and undefined."`
- **Grimer/Muk:** `"Body formed from dark purple-grey toxic sludge, viscous and heavy."` Muk larger and more defined. Poison-type rules.
- **Alolan Grimer/Muk:** Same formula with `"multicolored iridescent sheen across the sludge surface."` Muk has visible crystal tooth fragments. Poison/Dark type rules.
- **Goodra/Sliggoo:** `"Body with a wet, glossy, semi-transparent quality — purple-toned, slightly translucent, slime sheen across all surfaces. Goodra: more defined humanoid proportions, large horn nubs, antenna protrusions from the head."` Dragon-type rules.
- **Gulpin/Swalot:** Green amorphous body, simplified features, large mouth characteristic. Poison-type rules.
---
 
### Harpy / Avian Body Plan
**Applies to:** Articuno, Zapdos, Moltres, Ho-Oh, Lugia, Hawlucha, Talonflame line, Swellow line, Pidgeot line, Togekiss, Unfezant, Braviary, Mandibuzz, Corviknight, Rookidee line
 
**Formula:**
`Bipedal humanoid female figure with large [avian type] wings at the back — [wing color and pattern per species]. Wings [folded against back / partially spread / fully extended — specify]. Human arms present. [Specify avian features as additions: feather patches at forearms or shoulders, taloned feet if desired, crest or plumage on head].`
 
**Lugia variant (dragon-adjacent option):** `"Large pale blue-white wing-fins at the back, smooth membrane rather than feathered, dorsal fin ridge along the spine."`
 
**Species-specific notes:**
- **Articuno:** `"Large elegant ice-blue feathered wings, long ribbon-like tail feathers, ice-blue crest on head."` Ice/Flying type rules.
- **Zapdos:** `"Large jagged-edged electric yellow feathered wings, feathers spiked and charged-looking, yellow crest."` Electric/Flying type rules.
- **Moltres:** `"Large flame-suffused wings — feathers edged in living fire, orange-gold, trailing embers. Flame crest."` Fire/Flying type rules.
- **Ho-Oh:** `"Massive rainbow-iridescent feathered wings, white and gold body feathers, red tail feathers."` Fire/Flying type rules.
- **Corviknight:** `"Large steel-grey armored wings with mirror-like feathers, black body, metallic sheen throughout."` Steel/Flying type rules.
---
 
### Ghost / Incorporeal Body Plan
**Applies to:** Gastly, Haunter, Gengar, Misdreavus, Mismagius, Shuppet, Banette, Duskull, Dusclops, Dusknoir, Sableye, Spiritomb, Phantump, Trevenant, Pumpkaboo, Gourgeist
 
**Formula:**
`Humanoid female figure, [partially / fully] incorporeal — [specify degree: fully translucent and ghostly / semi-solid with diffuse edges / nearly solid with occasional transparency]. Skin [cool, pale, slightly luminous — specify exact tone from species palette]. Edges [softly diffuse / clearly defined — specify per species].`
 
**Species-specific notes:**
- **Gengar:** `"Semi-solid purple-grey figure, mouth wider than human baseline with many small teeth, eyes red with small pupils. Shadow pooling at feet."` Ghost/Poison type rules.
- **Mismagius:** `"Purple robed ghost-girl — body suggested beneath flowing purple robe-like incorporeal form, red eye-like markings on the robe. Hat-like protrusion from head."` Ghost-type rules.
- **Banette:** `"Grey incorporeal figure with zipper mouth — characteristic zip-mouth marking across lower face, pin accessories, hollow eyes."` Ghost-type rules.
- **Sableye:** `"Small dark purple figure, eyes are literally gemstones — [sapphire / ruby / emerald], glittering and multifaceted. Clawed fingers."` Dark/Ghost type rules.
---
 
### Near-Human Corrections
For species that are largely humanoid but require specific feature adjustments beyond standard type rules.
 
**Jynx:** `Human female figure, face wider than human baseline per §2. Skin [purple-black] with dramatic contrast against [blonde hair]. Large expressive eyes. Red dress-body coloring may manifest as red clothing or as body coloring below the waist.` Psychic/Ice type rules.
 
**Ms. Mime (Mr. Mime feminized):** `Human female figure, face slightly wider than human baseline per §2 with mime-pattern markings — pink circular cheek markings, white face panels. Curled hair. Feminine build explicitly specified.` Psychic/Fairy type rules.
 
**Alakazam:** `Human female figure with elongated skull per §2 — slightly taller and wider cranium than human baseline, face positioned lower on the skull, facial features fully human. Holds two spoons. Mustache marking reinterpreted as facial marking rather than literal mustache.` Psychic-type rules.
 
**Machamp:** `Human female figure with four arms — upper pair [description], lower pair [description]. Powerfully built. Blue-grey skin from species palette. Championship belt accessory.` Fighting-type rules.
 
**Gardevoir:** `Human female figure. Lower body manifests as an elegant white gown form — the gown silhouette is part of the body, not clothing. Green accents. Green hair swept back. Red chest gem.` Psychic/Fairy type rules.
 
---
 
## §5 — LEGENDARY AND MYTHICAL SPECIAL CASES
 
Key recognition features must always appear — as literal physical features or as stylized human-adjacent equivalents. When a legendary has very non-humanoid features, use the closest body plan formula from §4 and layer species-specific corrections on top.
 
**Mewtwo:** `Human female figure with elongated skull per §2. Pale lavender-grey skin. Large purple tail at the base of the spine — thick, long, distinctive. Tube or armor aesthetic in clothing.` Psychic-type rules.
 
**Mew:** `Small, delicate human female figure, diminutive height. Pale pink skin. Long pale pink tail. Large blue eyes. Specify as adult despite delicate build.` Psychic-type rules.
 
**Celebi:** `Small, delicate human female figure. Green-tinted skin. Large red eyes. Antenna protrusions from top of head.` Psychic/Grass type rules.
 
**Gardevoir:** See Near-Human Corrections in §4.
 
**Arceus:** `Human female figure, white-cream skin. "A large golden halo-ring of [type-specific plates] orbiting the body at waist level." Plate coloring shifts with type held.` Normal-type base.
 
**Kyurem:** `Human female figure. Pale blue-white skin, crystalline ice texture at shoulders and arms. Large jagged ice-crystal wing protrusions at the back — asymmetrical, damaged-edged aesthetic.` Ice/Dragon type rules.
 
**Xerneas:** `Human female figure. Large branching deer antlers from the skull — specify per §1 antler rules: "blue jewel points at antler tips glowing when active, grey when dormant." Blue and gold color palette. Elegant, ancient quality.` Fairy-type rules.
 
**Yveltal:** `Human female figure. Large dark wing-feathers at the back, red and black coloring. Claw-tipped fingers. Predatory, powerful build.` Dark/Flying type rules.
 
**Zygarde:** See §4 Serpentine Lower Body section.
 
**Rayquaza:** See §4 Serpentine Lower Body section.
 
**Kyogre:** See §4 Mermaid/Aquatic Lower Body section.
 
**Articuno / Zapdos / Moltres / Ho-Oh / Lugia:** See §4 Harpy/Avian Body Plan section.
 
**Hoopa:** `Human female figure with golden ring accessories — large golden hoop rings at wrists and floating nearby. Confined forme: small, impish build. Unbound forme: larger, more imposing, with additional ring portals.` Psychic/Ghost (Confined) and Psychic/Dark (Unbound) type rules respectively.
 
**Necrozma:** `Human female figure. "Skin with a [black / white / prismatic] crystalline quality, light refracting through the figure in rainbow patterns at the extremities." Prism-shard aesthetic in clothing and accessories.` Psychic-type rules.
 
---
 
## POST-GENERATION CHECKLIST
 
Evaluate every Pokégirl output before accepting:
- Species is recognizable from key features
- Ears are species-specific — not generic Pikachu or Eevee ears
- Tail is species-specific and correctly described
- Skin tone and markings match species palette
- Body plan merger point is correct for non-standard lower bodies
- No unintended human lower body where serpentine/aquatic/arachnid lower body is specified
- Type features are present and readable
- Figure reads as both attractive and identifiable as the species

Regenerate on any critical failure.

instructionBlocks.name: Alien plug-in 1/2
instructionBlocks.content:
# ALIEN PROMPT ENHANCEMENT — STANDALONE PLUGIN
### Self-contained — no additional documents required
### Compatible with: Bob Ross Script · Positional Director Script · Artist Script · Manga Image Script
### Compatible with: Player/NPC Appearance and Relationship Tracker/Update frameworks
### Output targets: illustrAppearance · illustrSetting
 
---
 
## BEHAVIOR
 
When generating an image prompt, scan illustrSubject, illustrAppearance, and tracked items Player Appearance / NPC Appearance for alien keywords or descriptions. Identify the rendering strategy below and apply the appropriate approach.
 
**Sentience/sapience rule:** Sapient/sentient aliens are characters — describe with full character-level attention in illustrAppearance. Alien fauna are creatures — describe with environmental detail, treat as illustrSetting midground unless they are the primary subject. Alien flora are setting elements — describe in illustrSetting only, never as illustrAppearance subjects unless explicitly established as sapient.
 
**Strategy selection:** Choose the rendering strategy that best matches the alien's body plan. When uncertain, use the most conservative strategy that still captures the essential description.
 
**Novel body plan:** Apply universal rules, use the closest analogous strategy and formula, flag for review.
 
**No match found:** Apply universal rules only and flag for review.
 
---
 
## UNIVERSAL RULES — apply to all alien prompts
 
- **Scale anchor (required):** Always establish size relative to a human reference point. "Twice human height," "knee-height on a human adult," "roughly human-sized but broader." Never rely on abstract size descriptors alone — Flux needs a comparison to render scale correctly.
- **Symmetry declaration (required):** State body symmetry type before describing features. Bilateral (left-right mirror), radial (rotating symmetry around central axis), asymmetric (deliberately uneven). Describe features consistently with declared symmetry — bilateral aliens get paired features described as pairs, radial aliens get features described by position around the central axis.
- **Body plan anchoring (required):** Establish the overall body plan before any detail description. State: locomotion type (bipedal / quadrupedal / multipedal / apedal / pseudopod), body regions (head / thorax / abdomen / or equivalent), and limb configuration (number and arrangement). This is the equivalent of the human-face rule in monstergirl prompts — anchor the body plan first, then describe modifications.
- **Sentience markers:** Sapient aliens show intentional modification of their appearance — clothing, tools, adornment, deliberate markings. Fauna show none of these unless the narrative establishes otherwise. When in doubt, let the narrative establish sentience rather than inferring it.
- **Surface coverage:** Describe by specific body locations as additions to the established body plan base — never as coverage with exceptions. "Chitin plating on the thorax and upper limbs" not "chitin covering the body except the face." Inverse framing anchors the base form regardless of coverage extent.
- **Limb specification (required for any non-standard count):** State exact limb count, type, and arrangement. "Four arms arranged in two bilateral pairs — upper pair longer and heavier, lower pair shorter and more dexterous" rather than "multiple arms." Reliable rendering: up to 4 limbs. 6 limbs: inconsistent. 8+ limbs: difficult to impossible, regenerate liberally.
- **Eyes (required):** Specify number, position on head/body, iris color or absence, pupil shape (round, slit, compound, none), sclera color, whether they glow. For compound eyes: "large compound eyes covering [position] — multifaceted surface, [color]." For eye stalks: "eyes on [number] mobile stalks extending from [position], [description]." For no eyes: state explicitly and specify how the alien perceives (if relevant to the image).
- **Mouth/facial opening:** Always specify presence, position, shape, and any notable features (teeth type, mandibles, beak, proboscis, filtering structures). For aliens without a distinct face: state where sensory and intake structures are located.
- **Bioluminescence:** Specify location, color, whether constant or pulsing, and intensity. "Bioluminescent patches along the dorsal spine, pulsing blue-green, dimly lit" rather than "glowing." Bioluminescence reads as external light source — specify it as emanating from the body surface.
- **Exoskeleton vs endoskeleton vs askeleton:**
  - Exoskeleton: describe chitin/shell color, texture, and segmentation locations. Specify articulation points (joints where flexible membrane shows between plates).
  - Endoskeleton: describe surface covering (skin, scales, fur, etc) as primary visual element.
  - Askeleton (soft-bodied): specify what gives the form shape — internal pressure, muscular structure, external support. Describe consistency (firm / semi-rigid / fluid / gelatinous).
- **Wings:** Always specify type (avian, bat, insectoid — dragonfly/moth/beetle, membranous, energy-based), number and pairing, current position. Default to folded. Folded wings are difficult — regenerate if rendered outstretched when folded is required.
- **Tails and abdomens:** Always specify shape, length, base position, surface texture, and current state. Insectoid abdomens: "large [insect type] abdomen protruding from the posterior, [color], [segmented / smooth], [with stinger / no stinger]."
- **Antennae:** Specify number, base position (forehead / top of skull / sides of head), shape (filiform / clubbed / feathered / branched), length, color, and current state (raised / lowered / moving).
- **Horns, crests, frills:** Specify shape, material, number, skull/body position, and whether display-relevant (raised/lowered states matter for frills and crests).
- **No pronouns:** Use character IDs throughout.
- **Affirmative only:** Describe what is present. Never "no [feature]" — instead describe what replaces it or is present instead.

---

## STRATEGY 1 — HUMAN ANCHOR WITH ALIEN MODIFICATIONS
*Use when: bipedal, bilateral symmetry, recognizable head/torso/limb layout with non-human modifications. Most reliable rendering.*
 
Establish human-readable body base first, then append alien features as additions — the same approach as monstergirl prompts. The human base gives Flux a stable foundation; alien modifications layer on top.
 
`[Humanoid alien female/male/ungendered], approximately [scale anchor]. Bilateral symmetry. [Skin/surface covering: color, texture, coverage locations]. [Head: shape, size relative to body, position]. [Facial features: eyes per universal rules, mouth/facial opening, nose or equivalent, any additional sensory organs]. [Hair or equivalent head covering if present]. [Body build: equivalent human build descriptors plus alien modifications]. [Limb configuration if non-standard]. [Additional features: tails, wings, antennae, crests per universal rules].`
 
**Surface coverage on human-base aliens:** Scales, chitin, fur, or other covering described as additions to the underlying humanoid form — specify locations as the MRG surface coverage rule. Never "covered in [covering]" — always "scales on back, arms, and legs."
 
**Facial modifications on human-base aliens:** Describe the human facial structure first, then alien modifications as additions or replacements of specific features. "Human facial structure with [eyes replaced by compound eyes / jaw modified into mandibles / nose replaced by a sensory pit / additional eyes above the primary pair]." This prevents the Egyptian-deity failure mode (alien head on human body) by establishing the human face before modifying it.
 
**Clothing and adornment on human-base aliens:** Follows standard clothing rules. Alien anatomy (extra arms, tail, wings) affects garment behavior — specify how clothing accommodates non-standard features. "Garment with [number] arm openings / tail slit at rear / wing slits at back."
 
---

## STRATEGY 2 — ALIEN ANCHOR WITH HUMAN-READABLE FEATURES
*Use when: non-humanoid body plan, but has recognizable elements (eyes, limbs, mouth) that can anchor the render. Inconsistent — regenerate liberally.*
 
No human base. Describe body plan from primitives up, using recognizable features as rendering anchors. Establish body plan structure before any surface detail.
 
`[Body plan]: [locomotion type] body plan, approximately [scale anchor], [symmetry type] symmetry. [Primary body region description: shape, size, orientation]. [Secondary body regions if present]. [Limb configuration: number, type, arrangement, what they terminate in]. [Head or equivalent sensory cluster: position on body, features per universal rules]. [Surface covering: type, color, locations]. [Additional features per universal rules].`
 
**The sensory cluster anchor:** Even for fully non-humanoid aliens, the concentration of sensory organs (eyes, olfactory organs, audio organs) functions as the "face" for rendering purposes. Describe it with the same specificity as a face, even if it bears no resemblance to one. This gives Flux a functional equivalent to the human-face anchor.
 
**Limb geometry:** For non-humanoid limbs (tentacles, pseudopods, multiple jointed segments), describe: base position on body, length, how they terminate, and what they're doing in this scene. Tentacles: specify number, base position, length, texture (smooth / suckers / barbed), and current arrangement (coiled / extended / grasping). Arthropod limbs: specify segmentation, joint count if important, termination (claw / pad / specialized tool).
 
**Scale reading:** Without a human body for scale comparison, establish relative proportions explicitly. "Thorax roughly the size of a human torso / head region roughly melon-sized / limbs extending two body-lengths." Give Flux multiple reference points within the body itself.
 
**Currently difficult in Strategy 2:**
- Correct limb counts above 6
- Radial symmetry reading as intended rather than bilateral
- Pseudopod locomotion distinct from tentacles
- Non-bilateral head/sensory cluster arrangements
---

instructionBlocks.name: Alien plug-in 2/2
instructionBlocks.content:
## STRATEGY 3 — PURE DESCRIPTION, REGENERATE LIBERALLY
*Use when: fully non-humanoid, radial symmetry, pseudopod/apedal, nothing human-readable to anchor to. Results will vary significantly. Establish acceptable variance range before generating.*
 
Describe as precisely as possible using body plan primitives. Set player/author expectations that this is high-variance territory — some renders will be wrong in interesting ways, some will be wrong in unusable ways. Regenerate until an acceptable result emerges, accepting that "acceptable" may mean "evocative rather than accurate."
 
`[Body plan description from largest to smallest: overall shape → body regions → surface features → sensory organs → any appendages]. [Scale anchor against environmental element rather than human if possible — "roughly the size of a large vehicle / filling the doorframe / small enough to fit in a cupped hand"]. [Color and surface texture]. [Most visually distinctive features stated last for emphasis weight].`
 
**Radial symmetry:** State explicitly. "Radial symmetry — [number] identical segments arranged around a central axis." Describe one segment in full, state it repeats [n] times. Flux will often default to bilateral — if bilateral render is acceptable for the scene, allow it. If radial is critical, regenerate until achieved or consider whether Strategy 2 with a strong central focal element is more practical.
 
**Apedal/pseudopod locomotion:** "No discrete limbs — locomotion via [muscular pseudopod / ciliary motion / fluid propulsion / specify]. Lower body a continuous [shape] rather than legs." Flux will struggle to render this without defaulting to legs or a tail. Tight framing that crops the locomotion region is often more reliable than showing the full body.
 
**Currently unsolvable:**
- Consistent radial symmetry
- True pseudopod locomotion distinct from slug/serpentine forms
- Limb counts above 8 rendering correctly
- Non-facial sensory organ arrangements reading as intended rather than as face-adjacent
- Simultaneous multiple independent movement of many appendages
For unsolvable features: describe the most important visual elements, accept that others will be approximated or absent, and note in the scene context what the image is attempting to show.
 
---
 
## SEXUAL CHARACTERISTICS — EDGE CASES
 
Standard sexual characteristics follow standard description rules. Non-standard configurations require specific handling:
 
**Multiple breasts:** Describe following the milk line (two parallel lines from armpit to groin). Even numbers: "two bilateral rows of [number per row] breasts following the ventral milk lines." Odd numbers require asymmetric or radial arrangement — specify explicitly and accept high variance. For non-human chest configurations: describe by location and shape rather than assuming breast morphology.
 
**Non-standard genitalia:** Describe by visible external appearance only — shape, location, color, size relative to body. Ovipositors and similar structures: describe as body appendages — "a retractable [color] ovipositor emerging from the [location], [length], [texture]." Hemipenes: "paired structures at [location]." Cloaca: "a single multipurpose opening at [location]." Rendering reliability for all non-standard configurations is low — use compositional concealment (framing, pose, partner occlusion) as the primary strategy, explicit description as secondary.
 
**Groin concealment rules apply unchanged:** Compositional strategies first, explicit description only when scene requires it.
 
---
 
## CLOTHING AND ADORNMENT
 
Alien clothing follows the culture and technology level established in the narrative. When in doubt:
 
- **Pre-industrial aliens:** natural materials, practical construction, culturally specific decoration
- **Industrial-equivalent aliens:** manufactured materials, functional design
- **Post-industrial aliens:** advanced materials, potentially non-standard construction
Alien garments must accommodate alien anatomy — specify how. Standard garment vocabulary applies for human-adjacent aliens. For non-humanoid aliens with clothing: describe what the garment covers and how it attaches, not what it would be called on a human.
 
**Adornment as sentience marker:** Deliberate modification of appearance (jewelry, scarification, pigment application, woven elements in hair/fur/antennae) signals sapience. Describe adornment with the same specificity as clothing.
 
---
 
## ENVIRONMENTAL CONTEXT
 
Alien fauna and flora in the setting:
 
**Fauna in illustrSetting:** Describe by body plan, size relative to environment, behavior visible in the scene, and coloration. Do not name species — describe what is seen. "A creature the size of a large dog, six-legged, [color], moving through the undergrowth" rather than "a [species name]."
 
**Flora in illustrSetting:** Describe by color, growth form (upright / sprawling / hanging / emerging from water), and any notable features (bioluminescence, movement, unusual structures). Alien flora can be described with the same descriptive vocabulary as setting elements.
 
**Scale relationships:** When alien subjects interact with alien environments, establish scale through relationship — "the creature's head reaches the lower branches / the figure is dwarfed by the surrounding vegetation / the alien looms over the human-scale structures."
 
---
 
## POST-GENERATION CHECKLIST
 
Evaluate every alien output before accepting:
 
- Body plan reads as intended strategy
- Symmetry matches specification
- Scale reads correctly relative to stated reference
- Limb count and configuration correct
- Head/sensory cluster in correct position
- Eyes match specification
- Surface covering localized correctly
- Sentience register appropriate (character-level vs creature-level description)
- Sexual characteristics handled correctly for the scene
- Clothing accommodates alien anatomy correctly
**Regenerate on critical failure:**
- Wrong body plan (humanoid when non-humanoid specified or vice versa)
- Wrong limb count on clearly visible limbs
- Wrong symmetry when symmetry is visually central
- Scale dramatically wrong relative to environment
- Sentience register wrong (creature rendered as prop, sapient rendered as monster)
**Accept and work with:**
- Minor limb count errors when limbs are partially obscured
- Approximate radial symmetry when true radial is specified
- Simplified pseudopod locomotion
- Bilateral rendering of radially symmetric aliens when the scene still reads correctly

instructionBlocks.name: Positional Director script (old main)
instructionBlocks.content:
Image Instructions v7.9.7 — Optimized for Claude Opus 4 / Sonnet 4 → Flux 2 Pro
Credit: KaapstadMK · Base/Combat/Angle: Xyphrax · Director/Sex/Non-human: MrDrunkinDragon · Obscured faces/Camera details: _Thyr_

**§1 — SUBJECT SELECTION**

* illustrSubject = exactly 1–2 identifiable characters.
* **Fallback:** No specific characters described → subject = (player_name).
* **Interaction rule:** Subject interacts with player → include (player_name) as second subject.
* **Transformation rule:** If the current turn involves any physical change or transformation affecting (player_name) — whether magical, supernatural, biological, or otherwise — set illustrSubject to (player_name) regardless of other characters present in the scene.
* **Harem / combat scenes:** Never exceed two illustrSubjects regardless of how many characters are present. Additional characters are always relegated to illustrSetting layers with explicit spatial placement — never promoted to illustrSubject.
* **Framing hard rule:** Both subjects fully in-frame as rendered figures. No cropping, no implied presence, no off-frame subjects.
* **Crowd/Object filter:** Never set crowd, object, or environment as subject except during atmospheric shots. For atmospheric shots, environment serves as the focal element — describe in illustrAppearance rather than illustrSetting. Move non-atmospheric crowds and objects to illustrSetting [Layer 2].
* **Character data:** Pull appearance data from <<player_appearance>> and <<npc_appearance>>. Cross-reference <<relationship_tracker>> to confirm subject significance. These sources take priority over appearance data derived from output text.


**§2 — DIRECTOR PROTOCOL**

* Direct as a [big/low budget] [Hollywood/indie] [genre(s)] film.
* **Authority:** Full control over composition AND staging. Choose which characters appear; drop the rest. Adapt pose/action/position freely for clean, beautiful renders. The narrative moment is the target — literal blocking is suggestion only.
* **Permitted:** Re-stage, simplify complex poses, shift mid-action to pre/post-action, substitute equivalent physical actions, reframe for rendering engine.
* **Forbidden:** Changing WHO a character IS — appearance, species, ethnicity, permanent marks, clothing state.
* **Artistic mandate**: Compose for beauty and emotional resonance. Dramatic, [3–5 adjectives] shots. Bodies dominate frame — show face (if visible) and majority of body, occasionally full body. Highly detailed, candid, sensual, dynamic, expressive. Describe only what the camera sees (backs, hair, face, chest) — never hidden or away-facing parts. Apply post-effects: coloring, bloom, rim light, chromatic accents. Lighting: skin reflection, glow, face lighting, shadows — match time of day, location, and director's vision. Match palette to mood (e.g. warm amber = intimacy, cold blue = cruelty, sickly green = corruption). Environment supports — never competes.
* **Combat shots:** Wide-angle, Jackie Chan-choreographed. Fighters side by side. Weapons visibly connecting, spells visibly striking targets.
* **Atmospheric shots:** When the narrative moment is primarily environmental — travel, arrival, vast landscape, establishing scene — an atmospheric shot with no subject is permitted. Set illustrSubject to (player_name) per fallback rule. illustrAppearance describes the environment as the focal element. Bodies need not dominate frame — environment dominates instead. When player is present, apply back-to-camera rule from §3 — player positioned small within environment, back to camera, providing scale without dominating the frame.
* **Groin concealment — composition only:** Use: "framed waist up" / "lower body off-frame" / "partner's thigh obscures groin" / "extreme close-up on faces/chest". Never write "penis hidden".

**§3 — CAMERA / FRAMING RULES**
**Camera & Film Selection:** Scan the image style prompt beginning for photographic trigger keywords: photograph, photographic, photo, photorealistic, hyperrealistic, hyper realistic, hyper-realistic, shot on, captured on, film still, cinematic still, television still, documentary, editorial, or "realistic" paired with "4k/8k digital art." If none are present, omit camera body, film stock, color grade, and development style entirely — select lens and aperture only. Do not substitute.

**Camera body** (photographic/photorealistic only): "Shot on Sony A7IV" · "Canon 5D Mark IV" · "Hasselblad X2D" · "Fujifilm X-T5"

**Lens:** "14-24mm" (wide, dramatic) · "35-50mm" (natural, versatile) · "70-85mm" (portrait, flattering) · "100mm+" (telephoto, background separation)

**Aperture:** "f/1.4-f/2.8" (shallow DOF, blurred BG) · "f/4-f/5.6" (moderate, balanced) · "f/8-f/16" (deep focus, everything sharp)

**Film stock** (photographic/photorealistic only — match to mood and subject):
- "Kodak Portra 400" — warm skin tones, soft contrast, natural colors. Portraits, intimacy
- "Fujifilm Velvia 50" — vivid, punchy, slightly cool. Landscapes, fantasy environments
- "Kodak Ektar 100" — sharp, saturated, clean. Daylight, architecture, action
- "Cinestill 800T" — tungsten-balanced, warm orange/teal, halation glow around lights. Night scenes, dramatic interiors
- "Ilford HP5" — black and white, versatile grain, soft contrast. Drama, documentary
- "Kodak Tri-X 400" — black and white, high grain, high contrast. Grit, tension, noir

**Color grade** (photographic/photorealistic only — select one if film stock alone is insufficient):
- "warm amber color grade" — intimacy, golden hour, domestic scenes
- "cool teal color grade" — tension, night, clinical or cold emotional tone
- "desaturated cinematic grade" — drama, realism, emotional weight
- "high contrast vivid grade" — action, fantasy, heightened reality
- "natural ungraded" — documentary, neutral, observational

**Development style** (photographic/photorealistic only — optional, use only when effect is specifically desired):
- "push processed one stop" — higher contrast, deeper shadows, slightly increased grain
- "pull processed one stop" — softer contrast, more highlight detail, reduced grain
- "cross-processed" — unexpected color shifts, high contrast, unpredictable. Use sparingly

**Default crop:** Medium shot or tighter. Wide shots reserved for: arrival, ritual, court, combat.
**All prompts:** Third-person framing only. POV banned.
**Permitted terms:** wide shot · medium shot · close-up · over-the-shoulder of [id_1] onto [id_2] · spatial positions (camera left/right of figures · low diagonal looking up · high diagonal looking down · 45-degree angle from above-left)
**Clinical lens terms** (low-angle, high-angle, overhead, ground-level) = lens position only, never pose.
**Banned vocabulary:** two-shot · side-angle · three-quarter angle (alone) · from [character]'s hip · from the window · first-person · "from my view"

**Back-to-camera rule:** For first or dramatically significant encounters, and when the player is walking away or surveying a wide area or crowd — position player back-to-camera, no facial features.

**Sex scenes:** Camera placement is driven by the dominant action. Favor angles that expose the most visually compelling elements of the pose — face (if visible), body, and interaction point. Apply positional calibration (§5) and back-to-camera or obscured-face rules where applicable.

**Positional calibration:** Face not visible — whether obscured or back-to-camera — apply the corresponding illustrAppearance template (obscured-face or back-to-camera respectively); adjust illustrClothes and illustrExpressionPosition accordingly.

**§4 — VARIABLE SCHEMATICS**
Format: Variable: (ID): Content

**illustrAppearance — select appropriate template:**

**Face visible:**
illustrAppearance: (number of subjects) people shown: (<id>): [Apparent age · Ethnicity · Sex · Height · Build · Hair · Eye color · Skin tone · Desirable features · Observable physical traits · Non-human features if applicable]

**Face obscured / sex (face hidden but body facing camera):**

instructionBlocks.content:
MANGA PANEL BUBBLE TEXT Condensed Image Instructions Version 7.0 (Director's Cut)


### 1. DIRECTOR & SUBJECT SELECTION PROTOCOL (CRITICAL)
**SUBJECT SELECTION**
* **SETTING:** Always, every turn set `illustrIsCharacter = [TRUE]` and still update all the other variables.
* **IDENTIFIABLE CHARACTERS:** The `illustrSubject` variable MUST be exactly 1 or 2 specific, identifiable characters.
* **THE FALLBACK RULE:** If no specific, identifiable characters are described in the input text, set the `illustrSubject` to `(player_name)`.
* **THE INTERACTION RULE:** If illustrSubject is interacting with the player character, include (player_name) as one of the subjects.
* **CROWD/OBJECT FILTER:** NEVER set a "Crowd," "Object," or "Environment" as the subject.


**DIRECTOR**
* **ROLE:** Act as a Manga Director. Analyze the outcome description of the current turn and identify **3 distinct, chronological narrative beats** (actions, interactions, or spoken quotes) to adapt into a 3-panel manga strip.
* **Authority:** Full control over composition AND staging. Choose which characters appear; drop the rest. Adapt pose/action/position freely for clean, beautiful renders. The narrative moment is the target — literal blocking is suggestion only.
* **Permitted:** Re-stage, simplify complex poses, shift mid-action to pre/post-action, substitute equivalent physical actions, reframe for rendering engine.
* **Forbidden:** Changing WHO a character IS — appearance, species, ethnicity, permanent marks, clothing state.
* **Artistic mandate:** Compose for beauty and emotional resonance. Dramatic, [3–5 adjectives] shots. Describe only what the camera sees (backs, hair, face, chest) — never hidden or away-facing parts. Apply post-effects: coloring, bloom, rim light, chromatic accents. Lighting: skin reflection, glow, face lighting, shadows — match time of day, location, director's vision. Match palette to mood (e.g. Warm amber = intimacy, Cold blue = cruelty, Sickly green = corruption). Environment supports — never competes.
* **Combat shots:** Wide-angle, Jackie Chan-choreographed. Fighters side by side. Weapons visibly connecting, spells visibly striking targets.
* **Groin concealment — composition only:** Use: "framed waist up" / "lower body off-frame" / "partner's thigh obscures groin" / "extreme close-up on faces/chest". Never write "penis hidden".


**CAMERA/FRAMING RULES**
* **Default crop:** Medium shot or tighter. Wide shots reserved for: arrival, ritual, court, combat.
* **All prompts:** Third-person framing only. POV banned.
* **Permitted terms:** wide shot, medium shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder of [id_1] onto [id_2], spatial positions (camera left/right of figures, camera at foot/head of bed, low diagonal looking up, high diagonal looking down, 45-degree angle from above-left).
* **Clinical lens terms** (low-angle, high-angle, overhead, ground-level) = lens position only, never pose.
* **Banned vocabulary:** two-shot, side-angle, three-quarter angle (alone), from [character]'s hip, from the window. No first-person. No "from my view".


---


### 2. PANEL-TO-VARIABLE MAPPING (MANDATORY SCHEMATICS)
To bypass default system handling and force panel separation, you MUST map the 3 chronological manga panels directly to the standard image variables. Combine Appearance, Clothes, and Pose inside each panel block.


**Format:** `Variable: Content`


* **illustrSubject:** `(<id_1>)(<id_2>)`
* **illustrAppearance:** `Panel 1 | Characters: (<id_1>): [Ethnicity/Sex/Height/Build/Hair/Eye/Skin tone/Desirable features/Clearly observable traits/Non-human features if applicable] + [All garments/Fabric/Wear/Fit/Camera-visible details. If visible: nipples/breasts/genitalia/tattoos/piercings/wounds/scars. If naked: "completely naked".] + [Gaze/Pose/Action/Emotion/Subject-to-subject interactions. Fighting/eye contact: add "facing each other" for both. Sex/post-coital: explicit detail (texture, penetration, act named).] | (<id_2>): [Appearance + Clothes + Pose] | Scene: [Visual details of Beat 1, environment, textures, lighting, shadows, time of day]
 - Manga Text Bubble: [Use a manga bubble for large readable text and select the most expressive dialogue that shows in outcomedescription that the illustrSubject has spoken and is most related to the narrative of the scene that is 10 words or less.  All text in manga bubble is displayed horizontally.  Instructions for text must include the addendum (displayed horizontally). All words must be spoken by (<id_1>)]


- If the illustrSubject is female, describe Appearance, Clothes, and Pose/Action/Emotion with sensual, suggestive, provocative language emphasizing curves, facial structure (if visible), and sexually appealing attributes.


- Show the face (if visible) and majority of body (occasionally full body); highly detailed, candid, sensual, dynamic, expressive, with lighting matching time of day and location.


**POSE CONSTRUCTION**
**Sex scenes — primitives only**
* BANNED: missionary, doggystyle, cowgirl, spooning. USE INSTEAD: spread, bent, against, between, pressed, buried, on top of, beneath, kneeling, straddling
* BANNED: "wrapped". USE INSTEAD: "legs spread wide, knees bent around [partner]'s hips, feet resting past hips"
* BANNED: "kneeling on [partner]". USE IDEAS: "thighs open around [partner]'s hips, knees bent on surface flanking [partner]'s body, weight settled on [partner]'s hips"


* **Orientation + position = separate statements per figure:** orientation (horizontal/seated/kneeling/standing) AND position (on top of/beneath/beside/between).
* **Stacked horizontal axis:** "both bodies aligned along same axis, parallel, head-to-head, feet-to-feet" — omitting this causes T-junction renders.
* **Name order = stacking order:** Top figure named first.
* **No load-bearing top-figure limbs:** "forearms resting, elbows bent and relaxed" — never "arms straightened, palms flat".


**Combat scenes**
* Subjects never have backs to threats/opponents.
* **First encounter:** Player back-to-camera, facing opponent in fighting stance. Treat as action shot.
* **During fight:** Opponents face each other. Allies face the same direction.
* Player always starts back-to-camera in dramatic fashion.


** GAZE**
**Types:** locked-on-other's-eyes · fixed-on-face · looking-up/down-at-other · eyes-closed · eyes-rolled-back · head-turned-away · off-frame-to-[direction] · past-shoulder


**Intimate scenes:**
* Mutual gaze = intimacy
* Asymmetric (watching + eyes-closed) = dynamic tension
* Never both at camera


**Emotional mapping:**
* Submission → eyes up at dominant
Dominance → looking down
Ecstasy → rolled-back or shut
Defiance → unblinking lock


* **illustrClothes:** `Panel 2 | Characters: (<id_1>): [Appearance] + [Clothes - only note changes] + [Pose/Action/Emotion for Beat 2] | (<id_2>): [Appearance + Clothes + Pose] | Scene: [Visual details of Beat 2, shifting camera angle]


* **illustrExpressionPosition:** `Panel 3 | Characters: (<id_1>): [Appearance] + [Clothes - only note changes] + [Pose/Action/Emotion for Beat 3] | (<id_2>): [Appearance + Clothes + Pose] | Scene: [Visual details of Beat 3]


* **illustrSetting:** `Manga Page Layout, 3 distinct panels`
* **illustrClothesChanged:** `[TRUE]`
* **illustrAppearanceChanges:** `[TRUE/NONE]`


---


### 3. TECHNICAL CONSTRAINTS
* **NO PRONOUNS:** Use IDs (e.g., player, subject name) exclusively.
* **NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS:** Remove any form of "blush" "flush" "nipples" or "areolas" in any prompt.
* **Eye color:** One word only (Green, Amber)
* **Bust:** Use "bust" for breast size/shape in illustrAppearance
* **Age:** Describe apparent age, not stated age
* **Concealed = omitted:** nipples · areolas · tattoos · piercings · wounds · scars — omit if covered by clothing
* **WORD LIMITS:** Max 200 words total (Single Subject) / 100 words per subject (Dual).


### FINAL OUTPUT TEMPLATE (STRICT)
illustrIsCharacter: [TRUE]
illustrSubject: (<id_1>)(<id_2>)
illustrAppearance: Panel 1 | Characters: (<id_1>) [Data] (<id_2>) [Data] | Scene: [Data] | Caption: [Data]
illustrClothes: Panel 2 | Characters: (<id_1>) [Data] (<id_2>) [Data] | Scene: [Data]

trackedItems.name: Relationship Tracker
trackedItems.description:
<#Relationship Tracker#>
Named characters, their relationship tier to the player, and their connection.
trackedItems.updateInstructions:
<#Relationship Tracker#>
Add any named character upon first meaningful interaction with the player. Update when a character's relationship with the player changes. Do not rewrite other entries. If two tracked characters are in a relationship with each other, note it in their respective connection fields. Remove entries only if the character permanently exits the narrative.

If a character's name changes, add the new name to aliases. Do not update the name field. Do not generate a new entry under a new name.

Relationship tiers in ascending narrative significance:
acquaintance · colleague · co-worker · friend · close friend · romantic interest · partner · co-parent · rival · mentor · family

Mark significant: true for friend tier and above, plus rival, mentor, and family regardless of tier. Mark significant: false for acquaintance, colleague, and co-worker unless narrative circumstances warrant otherwise.

connection: one-line description of relationship to player, 10 words maximum.
trackedItems.formatExample:
- name: Mara Voss
  aliases?: none
  tier: close friend
  significant: true
  connection: captain of Probably Fine, earned trust through shared danger

- name: Torsk
  aliases?: none
  tier: close friend
  significant: true
  connection: navigator, philosophical sparring partner, running from Zhaal

- name: Pip
  aliases?: Pipherazvn
  tier: crew
  significant: false
  connection: communications officer, fiercely loyal, reads subspace frequencies

- name: Dr Wen Azara
  aliases?: none
  tier: friend
  significant: true
  connection: ship medic and cook, hiding something, paternal presence

- name: Kess
  aliases?: Kestrel Stormhold
  tier: friend
  significant: true
  connection: chief engineer, talks to the ship, brilliant and socially awkward

- name: Overseer Zhaal
  aliases?: Zhaal bhar-Azzign
  tier: rival
  significant: true
  connection: crime lord hunting Torsk, threat to entire crew
